Photograph: Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic Television Hayden Panettiere, actor in Heroes and Nashville, dies aged 36 Panettiere’s death was announced by her father, who called her ‘an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy’ Hayden Panettiere – a life in pictures Sian Cain Mon 17 Aug 2026 00.39 EDT Last modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 01.44 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Hayden Panettiere, the actor known for her roles in television shows such as Heroes and Nashville , has died at the age of 36. Panettiere’s death was confirmed in a statement from her representative to the Guardian on Sunday night, after it was first reported on US network ABC News . No cause of death was given. Hayden Panettiere – a life in pictures Read more “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen,” her father, Skip Panettiere, said in a statement. He asked for privacy “as our family takes time to process this unimaginable loss”. View image in fullscreen Hayden Panettiere at the premiere of Pixar’s A Bug’s Life in Hollywood in 1998. Photograph: ZUMA Press, Inc./Alamy Born in 1989, Panettiere was a child star who began acting at just 11 months old, appearing in a toy commercial. She made her big screen debut as the voice of Dot in A Bug’s Life, aged nine. In 2000, she appeared in Remember the Titans. In 2004, she landed her first starring role as the daughter of Bill Pullman’s character in Tiger Cruise on the Disney Channel. Panettiere rose to global fame at the age of 17 as the invulnerable cheerleader Claire Bennet in Heroes, a series with the well-known, mysterious mantra: “Save the cheerleader, save the world.” The show was a hit and ran for four seasons between 2006 and 2010. View image in fullscreen Hayden Panettiere as Claire Bennet in Heroes. Photograph: NBC/NBCUniversal/Getty Images Panettiere also earned two Golden Globe nominations for her performance as the troubled country music star Juliette Barnes on Nashville. Eleven songs that Panettiere recorded for Nashville appeared on Billboard’s Hot Country Songs charts during the show’s run, including two featuring her co-star Connie Britton. She also appeared as Kirby Reed in 2011’s Scream 4 and 2023’s Scream VI. In 2014 she gave birth to her daughter, Kaya Klitschko, whom she had with her ex-fiance, the Ukrainian heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko. Panettiere gave full custody to Klitschko in 2018 in order to focus on recovering from what she called a “horrible cycle for years of battling depression and anxiety and alcoholism and substance abuse”. “I didn’t know where the alcoholism was ending and the postpartum was beginning,” Panettiere said in a 2022 interview. “And I ran myself pretty ragged.” She entered rehab in 2015 while filming Nashville, which ended informing some of the show’s storylines. “This hasn’t been easy and there were a lot of ups and downs,” Panettiere told People magazine in 2022 . “But I don’t regret even the ugliest things that have happened to me. I feel incredibly accomplished. And I feel like I have a second chance.” Earlier this year she published a memoir titled This is Me: A Reckoning, which touched on her struggles with fame, postpartum depression, addiction and recovery. In the book Panettiere wrote about the troubling link she made between acting and love: “Directors, fans, and Mom praised me endlessly for my over-the-top dramatic responses. Subconsciously, I began to associate catastrophe with adoration; people loved me because make-believe bad things happened to me.” In May, she gave an emotional interview to podcaster Jay Shetty about her daughter. “I will always want her here. I always miss her,” she said. “I always want to have my arms wrapped around her, but that’s just not the way life is right at this moment … I have faith that she is going to come to me and that we’re going to have an incredible relationship and bond and friendship that a lot of parents don’t get to have with their kids.” Panettiere is survived by her father, Skip Panettiere, and her mother, Lesley Vogel, who is also her former manager. Panettiere’s brother Jansen died suddenly in 2023 at the age of 28 from cardiomegaly – an enlarged heart – coupled with aortic valve complications. Ιωάννης Τσαμίχας By Ioannis Tsamichas, lawyer and President of the Hellenic-Italian Chamber of Commerce of Athens Share: Share via Facebook Share via Twitter Share via LinkedIn Share via Email Share via WhatsApp Copy Link Προσθέστε την «Ν» ως προτιμώμενη πηγή στο Google A country’s geography can be turned into a strategic advantage. Europe is at such a historic turning point, and Greece has an opportunity to become a key player in the new energy architecture. The Vertical Gas Corridor is not simply a route for transporting natural gas. It is a strategic European initiative that is reshaping the balance of energy security, strengthening interconnectivity and enhancing the geopolitical importance of Southeast Europe. As the European Union accelerates its drive to fully phase out Russian natural gas by September 2027, the need for diversified sources and reliable alternative supply routes is becoming even more critical. Greece now has the infrastructure and interconnections to play a greater role in Europe’s energy security. From energy periphery to the centre For decades, Greece and Southeast Europe were at the end of the main European energy routes. Today, the picture is changing. Greece is emerging as a major energy gateway to Southeast, Central and Eastern Europe. The Vertical Corridor creates an axis for two-way natural gas flows from south to north and vice versa. Its value lies in creating an interconnected, flexible and resilient regional energy system. DESFA, the Operator of the Greek national Natural Gas System, working with the transmission system operators of Greece, Bulgaria, Romania, Hungary, Slovakia, Moldova and Ukraine, is at the heart of this effort. This cooperation transcends national borders and strengthens Europe’s security of supply. DESFA as a strategic pillar DESFA’s role is steadily expanding. Through investment in infrastructure, increased cross-border capacity and the development of competitive capacity products, the operator is helping to unlock the full potential of the Vertical Corridor. ΔΙΑΒΑΣΤΕ ΕΠΙΣΗΣ Αιγαίο: Μπαράζ παραβάσεων και παραβιάσεων τη Δευτέρα από 5 τουρκικά αεροσκάφη – Μια αερομαχία Greek energy infrastructure is taking on a European mission, as the security of Greece’s system is now increasingly linked to the security of neighbouring markets. This is perhaps the most important element of the new reality: Greece is no longer simply an end destination for energy, but a critical hub within a broader European energy network. Greece and Italy: strategic partners Against this new energy geography, the relationship between Greece and Italy is acquiring particular strategic depth. The two countries are increasingly connected by shared European interests in energy and infrastructure. Greece lies at Europe’s southeastern gateway, while Italy is one of the continent’s most important economic and energy hubs. Their cooperation can strengthen an axis linking the Mediterranean with the Balkans and Central Europe. This relationship is not only geopolitical but also structural: Italian energy company Snam holds a stake in DESFA through the Senfluga consortium, while since February 2026 the operator has been headed by Maria Sferruzza, who brings extensive international experience in the global energy sector, having previously held a senior executive position at Snam. Her international energy-sector experience represents an important asset for Greek-European energy relations. A Chamber with a genuine strategic footprint In this new reality, the role of the Hellenic-Italian Chamber of Commerce of Athens also takes on particular importance. The Chamber is one of the key institutional and business players in bilateral economic relations, with a strong presence in the strategic energy sector. Among its members, supporting members and board members are leading companies in the energy and infrastructure sectors, including PPC, Edison, DESFA, HEDNO, IPTO, RENCO and TERNA. Its close cooperation with the Embassy of the Italian Republic in Athens further strengthens this mission. The Chamber thus acts as an important institutional catalyst, transforming the longstanding friendship between Greece and Italy into modern business partnerships, investment and strategic economic and energy cooperation. From corridor to regional platform The Vertical Corridor is now entering a new phase of commercial, regulatory and strategic maturity. The participation of North Macedonia through NOMAGAS and Serbia through Transportgas Srbija paves the way for expansion into the Western Balkans. Therefore, the Vertical Corridor is evolving from a cross-border natural gas route into an integrated regional platform for energy cooperation. It strengthens security of supply, diversifies sources and routes, enhances infrastructure resilience and supports the integration of energy markets. The new energy Europe The central message of the Vertical Corridor is ultimately simple: Europe’s energy security cannot depend on a single source, a single supplier or a single route. It requires diversification, interconnectivity and cooperation. This is where Greece’s major opportunity lies as it now occupies a pivotal position in the new European energy landscape. DESFA is one of the main pillars of this transition, while Italy is a natural and strategic partner. The Vertical Corridor can become the route through which Southeast Europe moves from the energy periphery to the heart of Europe. Greece is no longer the end of an energy route. It is the beginning of a new one. And this new route carries more than natural gas. It carries security, investment, competitiveness, geopolitical stability and European resilience. That is the true strategic role of the Vertical Corridor. And it is Greece’s great opportunity.
